A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MedMO and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. All seven appendix pages are identical in text and rendering, appearing on pages 15–21 in v1 and 16–22 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original MedMO benchmark results, training-stage and reward ablations, training dynamics, and qualitative predictions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds results for MedMO-4B-Next and MedMO-8B-Next.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–B retain the same architecture, four-stage pipeline, objectives, and bounding-box reward. However, v2 introduces undefined Next variants and describes the base model as reasoning without RL fine-tuning. The PDFs do not establish whether Next denotes existing training-stage checkpoints or a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The training corpus and evaluated VQA, text QA, report-generation, and grounding datasets remain unchanged. Next variants are evaluated within existing coverage; the additional QA breakdowns do not establish new domains or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same external comparison methods. Figure 1 drops InternVL3 from its summary display, but its corresponding benchmark results remain in the tables. Next models are additional proposed-model variants.

E3.justification: Table 1 expands selected rows from single scores to closed/all results for VQA-RAD and SLAKE and op4/op5 results for Medbullets. v2 also evaluates additional Next configurations. These extend the reported evaluation breakdowns, while Section 4.1 and the appendix training settings remain unchanged; rerunning existing experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The stage ablations in Figures 5–6, reward ablation in Table 4, appendix training analyses, and qualitative examples are retained unchanged. Removing Section 4.3.4's discussion does not remove its evidence: Figure 3 remains.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same seed information, including the example fixed seed 42, and Figure 16 retains its rolling-standard-deviation band. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 add extensive Next results, including MedMO-8B-Next's reported VQA average of 72.7, MIMIC-CXR CIDEr of 143.4, and grounding average of 56.8. Existing entries also change: MedMO-8B's MedQA score changes from 90.4 to 84.3, and Table 3's Lingshu Bacteria score changes from 0.00 to 10.8. These are substantial additions and revisions to reported results, not uniformly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Section 3 and the reward derivation and edge cases in Appendix A are unchanged. No theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive mathematical correction is added.

C1.justification: The central model contribution and introduction's contribution list remain unchanged. The abstract shifts from MedMO being within 1.9 points of Fleming on VQA to claiming Next leadership and competitive superiority for the smaller 4B-Next model. The conclusion adds an explicit best fully open-source medical multimodal foundation model claim.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the base model's stronger text-QA average as evidence of effective instruction tuning without RL overhead. It removes v1's suggestion that low IU-Xray RaTE may reflect annotation or evaluation differences. The catastrophic-forgetting limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds direct model-collection and GitHub links alongside the existing project-page information. Hardware, hyperparameters, training durations, and appendix implementation details remain unchanged, and no Next-specific training recipe is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 112 cited works are unchanged, apart from citation back-reference pagination. The methodological positioning around large-scale medical post-training and unified multimodal grounding is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and results narrative undergo substantial rewriting around four variants. Sections 4.3.1–4.3.3 reorganize the comparisons, report generation receives a more explicit heading and dataset-specific discussion, Section 4.3.4 is removed, and the conclusion is rewritten. Methods and appendices retain their structure and wording.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned with additional benchmark groups, Next bars, revised labels, and a longer caption. Tables 1–3 gain variant rows, Table 1 gains paired-result headers, and Tables 3–4 relocate as content reflows. The remaining figures and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful variant results, finer QA breakdowns, and direct resource links, but leaves the central Next variants technically undefined and introduces misleading comparisons. Figure 1 attributes a MedQA score of 66.1 to Fleming although Table 1 gives Fleming 53.7; its blanket Next-leadership claim also conflicts with the base model's higher text-QA average, 61.3 versus 60.1. The added evidence and these reproducibility and consistency problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
